# Overview

This tutorial shows how to create a functional annotation CSV file with gene IDs, descriptions, and annotations to be uploaded into the CONTENTO App. 

---

# Part 1: Source Genome Annotations

## Get Your Genome from NCBI

1. Go to [NCBI Assembly](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/assembly/)
2. Search for your genome accession (e.g., `GCF_000013465.1` for *Staphylococcus aureus* subsp. aureus FPR3757)
3. Click on the result and downoload the assembly in GFF3 format.
4. Unzip the file and save it in your working directory.

Alternative you can use the NCBI Datasets command-line interface (CLI) to download the GFF3 file:

```{bash}
# Install NCBI Datasets CLI if you haven't already
conda activate ncbi_datasets 

# Update the genome accession and directory as needed
GENOME_NAME="GCF_000013465.1" 
FILES_DIR="inst/extdata" 

# Update to download the desired files (genome sequence, GenBank flat file, GFF3...)
datasets download genome accession "$GENOME_NAME" \
            --include genome,gbff,gff3,seq-report \
            --filename "$FILES_DIR/$GENOME_NAME.zip"
```

File names and formats may vary, so make sure to check the downloaded files and adapt the code or rename the files to match the expected names in the code.

## Generate your own GFF3 file (Optional)

For genomes not available in NCBI, you can generate your own GFF3 file using Prokka [@Seemann2014] or similar annotation tools. Just make sure to include the necessary attributes (e.g., `locus_tag`, `product`, `go_process`) in the output GFF3.

---

# Part 2: Parse Annotation into CSV

```{r}
# Set up your R environment and read the GFF3 file. Adapt based on the GFF3 name and location

library(tidyverse)
library(here)

GENOME_NAME <- "GCF_000013465.1"
GENOMES_DIR <- here("inst/extdata")

gff_file <- file.path(GENOMES_DIR, paste0(GENOME_NAME, ".gff"))

# Read the GFF3 file into a data frame
gff_df <- read_delim(
  gff_file,
  delim = "\t",
  col_names = c("seqname", "source", "feature", "start", "end", "score", "strand", "frame", "attributes"),
  comment = "#",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Filter for CDS (protein-coding genes)
gff_cds <- gff_df %>%
  filter(feature == "CDS")

# Function to parse the attributes column of GFF3
parse_gff3_attributes <- function(attributes_string) {
  pairs <- str_split(attributes_string, ";")[[1]]
  
  attr_list <- list()
  
  for (pair in pairs) {
    if (pair == "") next
    
    parts <- str_split(pair, "=", n = 2)[[1]]
    
    if (length(parts) == 2) {
      key <- parts[1]
      value <- parts[2]
      attr_list[[key]] <- value
    }
  }
  
  return(attr_list)
}

# Apply the parsing function to the attributes column and create new columns for each key
annotations <- gff_cds %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    attr_list = list(parse_gff3_attributes(attributes))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Unnest all key=value pairs as columns
  unnest_wider(attr_list, names_repair = "universal")

# Save the annotations to a CSV file
output_file <- file.path(GENOMES_DIR, paste0(GENOME_NAME, "_annotations.csv"))
write_csv(annotations, output_file)
```
